senses.gloss: to accustom, train. Part. pass. לָמוּד, f. לְמוּדָה; pl. לְמוּדִים, לְמוּדִין; לְמוּדוֹת.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 4:3:1">Y. Ter. IV, 42ᵈ</cite> <he>כמות שהוא ל׳</he> according to what he is used to.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 4">Lev. R. s. 4</cite> <he>אינה ל׳ מבית וכ׳</he> she is not used (to handle T’rumah) from her father’s house.
Dem. IV, 4 ואם … ל׳ וכ׳ but if a priest or the poor are habitual guests at his table. Sifra K’dosh. Par. 3, ch. VI, v. לִימּוּד; a. fr.—3) to learn, study.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 2:5">Ab. II, 5</cite> <he>לא הביישן לָמֵד וכ׳</he> he who is bashful will not learn, nor can the hot-tempered teach, v. <cite ref="B00604"><he>בַּיְישָׁן</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 4:1">Ib. IV, 1</cite> <he>הלוֹמֵד מכל אדם</he> he who learns from everybody.

<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 4:20">Ib. 20</cite> <he>הל׳ ילד</he> he who studies at an early age; <he>הל׳ זקן</he> who begins to study at an advanced age. Ib. I, 9 <he>שמא … יִלְמְדוּ לשקר</he> lest through them (your intricate cross-examinations) they may be led to tell a lie.

<cite ref="Taanit 7a">Taan. 7ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Makkot 10a">Macc. 10ᵃ</cite> <he>הרבה לָמַדְתִּי וכ׳</he> I have learned much from my teachers, more from my colleagues, and most from my pupils; a. v. fr.—

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 71a">B. Mets. 71ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>הא לָמַדְתָּ</he> here you learn, i.e. this proves. [<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Esther 1:1">Targ. Esth. I, 1</cite> <he>מכאן אתה לָמֵד</he> from this you will learn.]

<cite ref="Shabbat 125b:8">Sabb. 125ᵇ</cite> <he>צאו ולַמְּדוּם</he> go out and place them (the building stones) in order (for sitting thereon the next day).—V. <cite ref="L00480"><he>לִימּוּדִים</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Horayot 13b:9">Hor. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>יְלַמֵּד אדם עצמו וכ׳</he> man should train his body (to relieve his bowels) early in the morning &c.
Nidd. 66ᵇ לעולם ילמד אדם בתוך וכ׳ man should make it a rule in his house; a. fr.—Part. pass. מְלוּמָּד, f. מְלוּמֶּדֶת; pl. מְלוּמָּדִים, מְלוּמָּדִין; מְלוּמָּדוֹת trained, experienced.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 109a:1">Snh. 109ᵃ</cite> top (in Chald. dict.) <he>דמל׳ בניסין הוא</he> for he has experience in miracles.
<cite ref="Taanit 25a">Taan. 25ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Sukkah 29a">Succ. 29ᵃ</cite> <he>מפני שמל׳ במכות הן</he> (not <he>במכותיהן</he>; Ms. M. <he>שרגילין</he>) because they (the Jews) have experience in afflictions; a. e.
<cite ref="Ketubot 50a:13">Keth. 50ᵃ</cite> <he>הלומד … ומְלַמְּדָהּ</he> he who studies the Law and teaches it.
<cite ref="Pesachim 112a:12">Pes. 112ᵃ</cite> <he>לַמְּדֵנִי תורה</he> teach me the Law; <he>איני מְלַמֶּדְךָ</he> I will not teach thee.
<cite ref="Pesachim 112a:12">Ib.</cite> <he>כשאתה מְלַמֵּד … לַמְּדֵהוּ וכ׳</he> when thou teachest thy son, teach him from a revised (correct) copy.
Snh. 19ᵇ אהרן ילד ומשה לי׳ וכ׳ Aaron begot (his sons), but Moses taught them, therefore they are recorded under his name; a. v. fr.—מְלַמֵּד תינוקות primary teacher.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 17b">Ib. 17ᵇ</cite>.
B. Bath. 21ᵃ מְלַמְּדֵי ת׳ teachers.—ל׳ זכות על to argue in favor of, to plead for; ל׳ חובה to plead against.

Sabb. 32ᵃ ואפי׳ … מְלַמְּדִים … ואחד מלמד עליו זכות ניצול and even if nine hundred … plead against him, and one (good deed) for him, he will be saved; a. v. fr.—Esp. (in textual interpret.) to lead, hint, throw light on. Sifra Emor Par. 4, ch. IV הייתי אומר תושב … בא שכיר ולי׳ על התושב וכ׳ I might have thought toshab (Lev. XXII, 10) meant one hired for a limited period; therefore sakhir (ibid.) comes in to throw light on toshab that it means one bought for life; Kidd. 4ᵃ; Yeb. 70ᵃ.—Sifra introd. יצא מן הכלל לְלַמֵּד is specified for the sake of illustration, v. כְּלָל.

<cite ref="Meilah 11b:3">Meïl. 11ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>שני כתובים … אין מְלַמְּדִין</he> two verses which coincide (teach the same), prove nothing, cannot serve as an illustration for similar cases; a. fr.

<cite ref="Gittin 24b">Gitt. 24ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Zevachim 2b:18">Zeb. 2ᵇ</cite> <he>בסופרים העשויים להִתְלַמֵּד וכ׳</he> it treats of scribes who are in the habit of writing documents merely for practice.
<cite ref="Gittin 60a:7">Gitt. 60ᵃ</cite> <he>לכתוב … להתל׳ בה</he> to write one portion of the Pentateuch for a child for practicing purposes; a. fr.
